title: Russian-occupied territories
capsule: Russian-occupied territories denotes the collection of regions in neighboring sovereign states held under Russian military control since 1992, including Transnistria in Moldova (from the 1992 Transnistria War), Abkhazia and South Ossetia in Georgia (formalized after the August 2008 Russo-Georgian War), and in Ukraine: Crimea and Sevastopol (annexed March 2014), parts of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts (from April 2014), and the partially-occupied Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts (from the February 2022 full-scale invasion, with annexation decrees signed 30 September 2022). All territories are internationally regarded as under military occupation in violation of the UN Charter; Russia disputes this characterization, recognizing several as independent states or Russian federal subjects. The cumulative area represents the largest forcible territorial changes in Europe since 1945.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The factual existence and approximate extents of these territories are well-documented by international monitoring bodies; precise front-line boundaries in Ukraine as of any given date are contested and continuously shifting.
